name: Write Your Own Git
tagline: A TypeScript/Node.js reimplementation of core Git internals — objects, the index, and the commands that create commits.
description:
Write Your Own Git is a from-scratch Git client written in TypeScript. It is not a wrapper around git. It reads and writes the same on-disk structures: zlib-compressed objects, tree and commit encoding, and the binary .git/index format, including TREE cache extensions.

The CLI (Commander) implements init, hash-object, cat-file, update-index/add, status, write-tree, commit-tree, commit, and diff. Tests run with Jest. The README still marks later challenge steps as unfinished, so this is a working internals implementation, not a drop-in replacement for Git.

coverImage.alt: Write Your Own Git — TypeScript CLI reimplementing Git objects, index, and core commands

problem: Using Git every day hides the actual model: blobs, trees, commits, refs, and a packed index. Without implementing those pieces, it is easy to treat version control as a black box instead of a content-addressed filesystem with a staging area.
approach: Implement the object database and index first, then layer commands on top. hash-object and cat-file prove encode/decode. update-index writes staging entries. write-tree and commit-tree build Git objects from that index. status and diff compare the worktree against the parsed index. Commander is the CLI; each command lives in its own module.
solution: A Node.js CLI that can initialize a repo, write blob objects, pretty-print objects, stage files, report worktree/index status, write trees, create commits, and show diffs. IndexParser reads .git/index headers, entries, and TREE extensions according to Git's documented index format.
outcome: The implemented commands and object/index parsers are covered by Jest tests. Remote protocol work from later steps of the original challenge is not claimed as complete.
features: hash-object — hash content and optionally write a Git object
cat-file — show object type or pretty-printed contents
update-index / add — register working-tree files in the index
status — compare worktree and staging area
write-tree — build a tree object from the current index
commit-tree and commit — create commit objects from trees
diff — show changes between index and working tree
Object encode/decode for Git blobs, trees, and commits
Binary .git/index parser with TREE cache-extension support
architecture: CLI (git.ts / Commander) → command modules → object encode/decode → IndexParser for .git/index → fileStatus for worktree vs index. Objects live as Git-compatible hashed files; the index is parsed as a binary structure rather than a text cache.
